name: Doodlebug
description: Hand-drawn GitHub stats cards for your README — stats, streaks, languages, trophies, banners. Built with Next.js + rough.js.

paragraphs: Doodlebug turns your GitHub activity into hand-drawn SVG cards — every stroke is generated with rough.js and a per-user seed, with real handwriting fonts embedded, so cards render anywhere (including GitHub READMEs) and no two look exactly alike.
Every README has the same stats card on it. They are competently drawn, identical to each other, and forgettable.

Doodlebug draws yours by hand instead. Nothing is a template: every rectangle, ring, arc and icon is generated stroke by stroke with rough.js from a seed derived from your username, so your card is wobbly in a way nobody else's is. The handwriting fonts are embedded in the SVG rather than linked, which is what lets the result survive GitHub's image proxy.

whatItDoes.text: Doodlebug turns your GitHub activity into hand-drawn SVG cards — every stroke is generated with rough.js and a per-user seed, with real handwriting fonts embedded, so cards render anywhere (including GitHub READMEs) and no two look exactly alike.

requirements.text: It is free, it needs no token to get started, and the whole thing — the card engine, the builder, the accounts, the caching — is in this repository.
Run it hosted, or self-host the lot.

Create a free Doodlebug account, save your GitHub username and (optionally) a personal access token: it is stored AES-256-GCM encrypted, only decrypted in memory to talk to api.github.com, and Doodlebug will use it whenever anyone loads a card for your username.
